wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

meanings.note: Used for women too. Common masculine noun meaning 'doctor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Она там взятки для врачей хранит.

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'вязывать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'would quit / wrap up'.

examples.text: Завязывал бы ты с картами, играть не умеешь.
examples.trans: You should quit cards, you do not know how to play.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и завязывать вовремя.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more needed'.

examples.trans: You need it more than I do.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.
Тошнит от = sick of. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'польный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('underground / secret').

examples.text: Это самое приличное подпольное казино Москвы.
examples.trans: This is the most respectable underground casino in Moscow.

examples.text: Как можно было потащить ребёнка в подпольное казино?
examples.trans: How could you drag our child to an underground casino?

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тащить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'dragged / carried'.

examples.text: Ты лучше скажи, куда Дениса потащили?
examples.trans: Better tell us where they dragged Denis!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и потащить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and dragged on time.

потерпеть.gloss: to be patient for a while, to endure

meanings.en: to be patient for a little while, to hold on
meanings.note: Often imperative: потерпи!. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терпеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be patient for a while, to endure', paired with 'терпеть'.

examples.text: Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: We need to be patient a little and work a bit.
Hang on for five more minutes.

examples.text: Послушай меня, Ваня. Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: Listen to me, Vanya. We need to be patient a little and work a bit.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тренироваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'practice'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и потренироваться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and practice on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют потренироваться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to practice.

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

meanings.note: 'Проходите!' = Come in! (inviting a guest)

Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go through; to come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'effect', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Молодой человек, постойте, это для психологического эффекта!
examples.trans: Young man, hold on, this is for psychological effect!

examples.text: Что вы делаете, немедленно уберите ваши руки!
examples.trans: What are you doing, take your hands off me immediately!

meanings.note: Plural: дети. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'child' in everyday Russian.
Жать руку = to shake hands. Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to save, to rescue', paired with 'спасать'.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: to remove, to take away, to cut out
meanings.note: A room. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remove, to take away; to tidy up', paired with 'убирать'.

A room. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remove, to take away; to tidy up', paired with 'убирать'.

examples.text: Ты можешь убрать весь этот шум?

examples.text: Так, ты можешь убрать весь этот шум? Нам нужен только Аникеев.
examples.trans: Right, can you cut out all this noise? We only need Anikeev.

уметь.gloss: to know how to, to be able to

meanings.note: + infinitive: a learned skill. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know how to, to be able to', paired with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
